Module is set up and verified across all target OSes.

```
go.mod                          module github.com/example/syscli (go 1.27, golang.org/x/sys v0.48.0)
main.go                         CLI entrypoint
internal/syscallx/
  syscallx.go                   package docs: x/sys + raw-syscall escape hatches
  version_unix.go               //go:build unix    -> unix.Uname (Linux/macOS/BSD)
  version_windows.go            //go:build windows -> ntdll!RtlGetVersion via LazySystemDLL
  version_other.go              //go:build !unix && !windows -> error stub
```

Key decisions:
- `golang.org/x/sys` for OS bindings, split by build tags; `unix` tag covers Linux+macOS, avoiding duplicate files.
- Windows uses `windows.NewLazySystemDLL("ntdll.dll")` + `RtlGetVersion` (`main.go` -> `syscallx.KernelVersion`), demonstrating the raw-DLL path when x/sys lacks a binding.
- Fallback file keeps non-Unix/non-Windows targets compiling.

Verified: `go vet`, plus `GOOS` builds for linux, darwin, windows, and fallback plan9/wasip1. `go run .` prints `Linux 7.0.14-linuxkit aarch64`.
